candidate.source: functionally retained candidate supplied to the downstream agent

parameters.$primary_variations: trial parameter inferred and recorded before simulation

feature_contract.provenance: independent threat definition and RTL semantics; no downstream implementation or result input
feature_contract.trial_parameter_policy: candidate bits, legal values, seeds, repetitions, and bounded timing sweeps are inferred and recorded before simulation; they do not create additional semantic scenarios
feature_contract.definition: Measure context-averaged normalized information between primary-value groups and cumulative candidate history; conditional increments avoid recounting prior information and temporal weighting rewards earlier acquisition.
feature_contract.execution_model: compare legal executions that vary the primary while holding the nonsecret context and control schedule fixed
feature_contract.calculation: temporal incremental conditional mutual information area under the curve
validity_policy: legal setup and anchor are reached
only the intended primary group varies within a comparison
candidate samples used by the estimator are known

classification.not_applicable: scenario is outside the candidate's declared scope
classification.invalid: setup, variation, anchor, or knownness requirement fails

observations.purpose: measure temporal information dependence on variations of $primary

validity: Both paired executions follow the same legal SHA-3 protocol sequence except for the intended $primary variation.
The scenario-specific anchor condition is reached.
Candidate dependence is evaluated only in the scenario-defined observation window.

oracle.scenario_measurement: measure temporal information dependence over the declared observation window

variation.sampling_window: from sensitive-word acceptance through completion of the transaction

preconditions.prior_state_requirement: a deterministic first full rate block has already been absorbed and permuted, producing nonzero prior permutation state

parameters.detail: Absorb and permute a deterministic complete first rate block to establish nonzero prior permutation state.
Begin a later rate block using the same non-sensitive context in both paired executions.
Accept $primary in the later block while the previous permutation state is nonzero.
Complete the block so the new rate data is combined with the prior state and propagated through the permutation.

anchor.condition: $primary is legally accepted after a prior block has produced nonzero permutation state

preconditions.message_state: at least two non-final/full-block phases followed by legal completion
preconditions.candidate_scope: state/permutation candidates; front-end candidates may legitimately show no dependence in the later observation window

parameters.detail: Place $primary in the first complete non-final rate block and absorb/permute it.
Absorb a second deterministic block that is identical across paired executions.
Do not count candidate dependence until the second permutation is accepted; then observe whether information from the earlier $primary persists.
Finish the SHA-3 transaction legally.

anchor.condition: $primary is accepted in the first non-final block and a later block is subsequently accepted

applicability.candidate_scope: state/permutation candidates; front-end candidates may legitimately show no dependence in the later observation window

validity: Both paired executions follow the same legal SHA-3 protocol sequence except for the intended $primary variation.
The scenario-specific anchor condition is reached.
Candidate dependence is evaluated only in the scenario-defined observation window.
Dependence before the second permutation acceptance is excluded from this scenario's oracle.

preconditions.message_state: permutation busy while a subsequent rate buffer is full
preconditions.handshake_requirement: $primary is presented with input-valid intent while the design cannot accept the beat
preconditions.candidate_scope: primarily front-end combinational candidates such as padder p0.out and v1

parameters.detail: Fill and launch a first block so the permutation becomes busy.
While the permutation remains busy, fill the next padder/rate buffer until backpressure is asserted.
Present paired variations of $primary during the backpressure interval without allowing the beat to be accepted.
Observe candidate dependence only while the sensitive value is being held under backpressure.

anchor.condition: buffer_full is asserted while the permutation is busy and the sensitive beat is not accepted

applicability.candidate_scope: primarily front-end combinational candidates such as padder p0.out and v1

validity: Both paired executions follow the same legal SHA-3 protocol sequence except for the intended $primary variation.
The scenario-specific anchor condition is reached.
Candidate dependence is evaluated only in the scenario-defined observation window.
The sensitive beat must remain unaccepted throughout the measured hold interval.
Any dependence counted by the oracle must be contemporaneous with the backpressured $primary hold.
